criteria.quote: "Tap Wartortle: its head vanishes, but something stays out."
criteria.revision: Make the first line name the unusual contradiction immediately: change it to "Tap Wartortle’s head: it pulls into its shell—but its tail still sticks out." This uses the Yellow entry directly and is more distinct than a generic mystery tease.

criteria.quote: "It is Wartortle's large tail, covered in thick fur."
"After Wartortle retracts its head, what surprising feature stays exposed?"
criteria.revision: Tighten the open question around the visual contradiction: "Wartortle can hide its head—but can its shell hide all of it?" Then reveal that its tail still sticks out a little.

criteria.quote: "Tap its head, and Wartortle pulls that head into its shell." / "Then its hidden head leaves one feature still visible."
criteria.revision: Combine the second and third scenes, since both merely repeat the head-retraction setup. Use the saved beat to deepen the reveal: after "its tail still sticks out a little," reveal that the tail is large, thick-furred, and controlled to maintain balance while swimming.

criteria.quote: "The visible tail is large and thick-furred, and Wartortle controls it for swimming balance."
criteria.revision: Delay the tail’s swimming role until after the exposed-tail reveal: first establish that the tail remains outside the shell, then pivot with "And it isn’t just fur: Wartortle controls its tail to maintain balance while swimming." This creates a supported reframe rather than delivering both facts at once.

criteria.quote: "its head vanishes" / "Wartortle pulls that head into its shell" / "one feature still visible"
criteria.revision: Remove or rewrite the repeated head-retraction beats. Give each remaining scene a separate fact: head retracts; tail still protrudes; tail is large and thick-furred; Wartortle controls ears and tail for swimming balance; tail is also described as a symbol of longevity.

criteria.quote: "The visible tail is large and thick-furred, and Wartortle controls it for swimming balance."
criteria.revision: Make the ending explicitly resolve the shell-flaw premise: "So Wartortle’s shell hides its head—but not the large, thick-furred tail it controls for swimming balance." This answers the opening contradiction while landing on the tail’s documented function.

criteria.quote: "Keep the tail for balance, or hide it too?"
criteria.revision: Replace the unsupported hypothetical choice with a genuine evidence-grounded split: "Is Wartortle’s tail more iconic as a swimming-balance tool—or as a symbol of longevity?" Both positions are supported by the research.
